cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Win the Smaller Concession
cards.instruction: Get one small surrender, then use its logic to make the larger claim harder to defend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my plant beside your pot on the windowsill. Can this one stay?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One small plant, yes. My pot's empty; I'm drying it after washing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, a drying place. Mine's been overwatered, so the second one should come here too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The second one's enormous. It will block the light from the first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then swap their positions at lunchtime. You agreed they can dry here; neither should lose its turn in the sun.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies pot placement as plant permission; A3 turns B2 drying reason into wider rights; A5 reuses B4 light objection to demand shared rotation.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 grants one/drying purpose leads A3 second plant; B4 light blockage leads A5 swapping, but only one plant was described as overwatered.

relationship.evidence: B4 wants the approved plant to receive light, a practical objection A can exploit.

heightening.evidence: A5 tries to make B4 concern justify care of both plants.

specificity.evidence: A1 sill/pots and B4 large second plant are clear; A3 moisture condition is singular.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 sunlight turn is a direct practical demand, not abstract principle talk.
